text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: You are a 22-year-old male with a known history of tics currently taking haloperidol. You have developed a high fever over the last two days accompanied by altered mentation, but you deny chills, rigors, headache, or other focal neurological symptoms. Given your medication history and presentation, are you experiencing muscle stiffness or difficulty moving your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS). The clinical picture of fever, altered mentation, generalized rigidity, and profuse sweating in a patient taking haloperidol is diagnostic for NMS. Please ensure the patient is transferred to the ICU immediately for supportive care and dantrolene administration.
